justification: MCP-1 (CCL2) is a chemokine that recruits monocytes/macrophages to sites of inflammation. Lyon 2016 showed MCP-1 inversely associated with complex attention (t=-2.63 p=.011) and psychomotor speed at 2yr post-chemo in breast cancer patients. Also reported by Vardy 2015 (CRC: IL-6 IL-8 IL-10 IL-12 correlated with processing speed). MCP-1 is a distinct inflammatory mediator not captured by IL-6 CRP or TNF nodes. Active area of CRCI research. Evidence: ≥2 neuroinflammation papers.
example_instruments: ELISA; Luminex multiplex cytokine panel; MSD V-PLEX
source_quote: MCP-1 was inversely associated with complex attention (t=-2.63 p=.011) at two years post-chemotherapy (Lyon 2016)

justification: sTNF-RII is a soluble decoy receptor reflecting chronic TNF pathway activation. Distinct from TNF-α itself — reflects sustained rather than acute inflammation. Hoogland 2019 showed sTNF-RII × Time predicted worse attention (b=-5.23 p<.01) and memory in HCT patients. Currently proxied to NODE_BIO_TNF but mechanistically distinct (receptor vs ligand). Evidence: ≥1 neuroinflammation paper with dedicated sTNF-RII measurement.
source_quote: Patients with greater increases in sTNF-RII demonstrated worse attention (b=-5.23 p<.01) over time (Hoogland 2019)

justification: IL-8 (CXCL8) is a pro-inflammatory chemokine involved in neutrophil recruitment. Trudeau 2025 showed IL-8 associated with better multitasking among AYAC (p=0.004). Vardy 2015 reported IL-8 among cytokines correlated with reduced processing speed (rho=0.18-0.40) in CRC patients. Distinct inflammatory mediator with chemotactic function different from IL-6/TNF/CRP. Evidence: ≥2 neuroinflammation papers.
example_instruments: ELISA; Luminex multiplex cytokine panel; MSD V-PLEX
source_quote: IL-8 was associated with better multitasking among AYAC (p=0.004) (Trudeau 2025); IL-8 correlated with reduced processing speed (rho=0.18-0.40) (Vardy 2015)

justification: IL-10 is an anti-inflammatory cytokine that counterbalances pro-inflammatory cascades. Trudeau 2025 showed lower IL-10 associated with worse self-perceived cognition among AYAC (p=0.015) and with higher BDNF (p=0.002). Vardy 2015 reported IL-10 among cytokines associated with processing speed in CRC patients. IL-10's anti-inflammatory role is mechanistically distinct from pro-inflammatory IL-6/TNF and needs separate representation to capture opposing regulatory effects on cognition. Evidence: ≥2 neuroinflammation papers.
source_quote: Lower IL-10 was significantly associated with worse self-perceived cognition among AYAC (p=0.015) (Trudeau 2025); IL-10 correlated with processing speed in CRC (Vardy 2015)

justification: IFN-γ is a pro-inflammatory cytokine produced by T cells and NK cells. Trudeau 2025 showed IFN-γ significantly associated with lower BDNF among healthy controls (p=0.016). IFN-γ activates the kynurenine pathway (tryptophan → quinolinic acid) which is a key mechanism in neuroinflammation-mediated cognitive decline. Distinct from IL-6/TNF signaling. Evidence: 1 neuroinflammation paper + strong mechanistic rationale (kynurenine pathway).
source_quote: Lower IFN-γ was significantly associated with higher BDNF levels among NC (p=0.016) (Trudeau 2025)

justification: IL-4 is a Th2 cytokine with anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties. Trudeau 2025 showed higher IL-4 significantly associated with higher BDNF among AYAC (p=0.003). IL-4 promotes alternative microglial activation (M2 phenotype) which can be neuroprotective. Represents the Th2/anti-inflammatory arm of immune balance relevant to CRCI. Evidence: 1 paper with dedicated finding; mechanistically important for immune balance.
source_quote: Higher IL-4 was significantly associated with higher BDNF among AYAC (p=0.003) (Trudeau 2025)

justification: Multitasking/cognitive flexibility is a distinct cognitive domain assessed by CANTAB Multitasking Test and other set-shifting paradigms. Trudeau 2025 reports IL-6→worse multitasking (p=0.026) IL-8→better multitasking (p=0.004) and TNF-α→worse multitasking (p=0.025) among AYAC. Not equivalent to working memory (maintenance/manipulation) or executive planning (novel problem-solving). Currently no node captures multitasking/set-shifting. Closest existing: NODE_COG_EXEC_PLANNING but executive planning is specifically about planning/sequencing. Multitasking involves task-switching and divided attention which are functionally and anatomically distinct (prefrontal-parietal switching networks vs. dorsolateral PFC planning). Evidence: 1 paper with 3 significant findings referencing this domain.
example_instruments: CANTAB Multitasking Test; Wisconsin Card Sorting Test; Trail Making Test Part B (set-shifting aspect)
source_quote: Among AYAC higher IL-6 was associated with worse multitasking (p=0.026); IL-8 with better multitasking (p=0.004); TNF-α with worse multitasking (p=0.025) (Trudeau 2025)
